heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Bulgaria
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to EOR & PEO in Bulgaria
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for EOR & PEO in Bulgaria.

steps.title: Requirement Analysis
steps.description: Define role scope and salary. EOR calculates total cost including 19-20% social security.

steps.title: Medical Exam
steps.description: Candidate undergoes mandatory initial medical check-up (Predvaritelen meditsinski pregled) before contract signing.

steps.title: Contract Signing
steps.description: Sign 'Trudov Dogovor' (Employment Contract) in Bulgarian. English translation is for reference only.

steps.title: NRA Registration
steps.description: EOR registers the contract with the National Revenue Agency (NRA) within 3 days of signing.

steps.title: Safety Instruction
steps.description: Employee completes mandatory initial health and safety instruction on the first working day.

items.title: Written Contract
items.text: Employment contracts must be in writing and registered with the NRA to be valid.

items.title: Probation Period
items.text: Maximum 6 months. Can be terminated without notice within this period if agreed.

items.title: Medical Check
items.text: Mandatory prior to employment. Failure to provide results invalidates the hiring process.

faqs.question: Is a 13th month salary mandatory?
faqs.answer: No, it is not legally required but is a common discretionary bonus.

faqs.question: What is the standard notice period?
faqs.answer: Typically 30 days, but can be agreed up to 3 months for mutual termination.

faqs.question: Are background checks legal?
faqs.answer: Allowed but restricted. Criminal record checks are common for specific roles (e.g., finance).

items.title: Currency Peg
items.text: The Bulgarian Lev (BGN) is pegged to the Euro at 1.95583 BGN = 1 EUR.

items.title: Cyrillic Script
items.text: Bulgaria is the birthplace of the Cyrillic alphabet; official documents must be in Bulgarian.

items.title: Vacation
items.text: Minimum 20 working days of paid annual leave.

steps.title: Data Collection
steps.description: Gather timesheets and bonus data (monthly). Adjust for sick leave (Bolnichni) and vacation.

steps.title: Calculations
steps.description: Apply Social Security (~13.78% employee / ~19% employer) and Flat Income Tax (10%).

steps.title: Submission
steps.description: Submit 'Declaration 1' (insured persons) and 'Declaration 6' (liabilities) to NRA electronically.

steps.title: Payment
steps.description: Net salary transfer in BGN or EUR (if agreed), tax payment to budget (must be BGN).

steps.title: Payslips
steps.description: Distribute payslips (Fishove) securely to employees.

items.title: Flat Tax
items.text: Bulgaria offers a flat 10% personal income tax rate, one of the lowest in the EU.

items.title: Social Security Cap
items.text: Contributions are capped at a monthly income of BGN 3,750 (2024), rising to BGN 4,130 (2025).

items.title: QES Requirement
items.text: Qualified Electronic Signature (QES) is required for all NRA filings.

faqs.question: Can we pay salaries in EUR?
faqs.answer: Net salary can be EUR, but standard practice and statutory payments must be BGN.

faqs.question: Are electronic payslips legal?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the employee has given consent.

faqs.question: When is tax due?
faqs.answer: Tax and social security payments are due by the 25th of the following month.

items.title: Declaration 1 & 6
items.text: These are the two critical monthly returns that must match payments exactly.

items.title: Sickness Benefit
items.text: First 3 days paid by employer (70%), remainder by National Social Security Institute (NOI).

items.title: Banking
items.text: SEPA transfers work, but local BGN transfers (RINGS/BISERA) are faster/cheaper.

steps.title: Gross Salary
steps.description: Start with the agreed monthly gross salary (BGN).

steps.title: Employee Deductions
steps.description: Deduct Pension (6.58%), Health (3.2%), PD (0.9%), Unemployment (0.4%), etc. ~13.78% total (capped at BGN 3,750).

steps.title: Income Tax
steps.description: Apply flat 10% tax on the taxable base (Gross - Social Security).

steps.title: Net Salary
steps.description: Resulting amount payable to the employee.

steps.title: Employer Contributions
steps.description: Add ~18.92% on top of Gross (Pension, Health, Accident, etc.) to get Total Cost.

items.title: Max Base
items.text: Social security contributions are capped at a maximum monthly income of BGN 3,750 (2024).

items.title: Minimum Wage
items.text: The minimum monthly wage is BGN 933 (as of Jan 2024).

items.title: Food Vouchers
items.text: Tax-exempt food vouchers up to BGN 200 per month are a popular benefit.

faqs.question: Is there a 13th salary?
faqs.answer: Not mandatory by law, but commonly offered as a Christmas bonus or performance bonus.

faqs.question: How is overtime paid?
faqs.answer: Overtime is generally prohibited but if permitted (e.g. shifts), paid at 150-175% rates.

faqs.question: When are taxes due?
faqs.answer: Taxes and social security must be paid by the 25th of the following month.

items.title: Leaves
items.text: Minimum 20 days paid annual leave. Sick leave first 2 days paid by employer (70%).

items.title: Maternity
items.text: Bulgaria has one of the most generous maternity leaves (410 days, 90% of salary).

items.title: Probation
items.text: Up to 6 months. Employer can terminate without notice during probation unless agreed otherwise.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Bulgaria
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Incorporation in Bulgaria
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Incorporation in Bulgaria.

steps.title: Reserve Name
steps.description: Optional: Reserve company name with the Commercial Register (BGN 20-40).

steps.title: Capital Deposit
steps.description: Open a fundraising account (nabiratelna smetka) and deposit min capital (2 BGN for OOD/EOOD).

steps.title: Documents
steps.description: Prepare Articles of Association, Specimen Signatures, and declarations.

steps.title: Registration
steps.description: File application with the Commercial Register (Registry Agency) physically or electronically.

steps.title: VAT & Banking
steps.description: Convert account to current account and register for VAT if threshold is met (>100k turnover) or voluntary.

items.title: Structure Types
items.text: EOOD (Single-member LLC) and OOD (Multi-member LLC) are the most common forms.

items.title: Low Capital
items.text: Minimum capital requirement is just BGN 2 (~€1).

items.title: Remote Setup
items.text: Possible via Power of Attorney (POA), though bank account opening may require scrutiny.

faqs.question: Can a foreigner own 100%?
faqs.answer: Yes, full foreign ownership is permitted.

faqs.question: Is a physical office required?
faqs.answer: A registered address is required, but it can be a virtual office.

faqs.question: How long does it take?
faqs.answer: 3-5 business days for registry if documents are in order.

items.title: Tax System
items.text: Flat 10% Corporate Income Tax (CIT) applies to worldwide income of residents.

items.title: UIC / EIK
items.text: The Unified Identification Code (EIK) is your company's permanent ID.

items.title: EU Market
items.text: Incorporation grants access to the EU single market.

heroData.title: Staffing in Bulgaria
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Staffing in Bulgaria
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Staffing in Bulgaria.

steps.title: Sourcing
steps.description: Leverage local job boards (Jobs.bg, Noble Hire) and LinkedIn to find talent.

steps.title: Screening
steps.description: Conduct initial interviews and check for English proficiency (widely high).

steps.title: Assessment
steps.description: Administer technical tests or case studies relevant to the role.

steps.title: Offer & Contract
steps.description: Extend offer. Written employment contract is mandatory per Labor Code.

steps.title: Onboarding
steps.description: Collect Medical Certificate and Criminal Record Certificate (Svidetelstvo za sadimost).

items.title: Tech Hub
items.text: Sofia is a mature tech hub (Java, Python, JS, PHP) with competitive rates.

items.title: Notice Period
items.text: Typically 1-3 months, but mutual agreement for early exit is common.

items.title: Remote Work
items.text: Remote work is regulated and requires a specific annex to the employment contract.

faqs.question: Can we hire independent contractors?
faqs.answer: Yes, via Service Agreement, but strict criteria apply to avoid hidden employment.

faqs.question: What is the probation period?
faqs.answer: Maximum 6 months can be agreed upon in the contract.

faqs.question: Is non-compete enforceable?
faqs.answer: Generally difficult to enforce and requires compensation payment.

items.title: Blue Card
items.text: Bulgaria offers EU Blue Card for highly skilled non-EU nationals.

items.title: Education
items.text: Strong technical universities produce high-quality engineering talent.

items.title: English
items.text: English proficiency is excellent among the younger workforce.

heroData.title: HRIS in Bulgaria
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to HRIS in Bulgaria
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for HRIS in Bulgaria.

steps.title: Needs Assessment
steps.description: Define scope: Payroll integration, time & attendance, performance management.

steps.title: Vendor Selection
steps.description: Evaluate local (HeRMeS, Smart HR) vs global (Workday, SuccessFactors) providers.

steps.title: Localization Check
steps.description: Verify NRA reporting capabilities and Bulgarian language interface.

steps.title: data Migration
steps.description: Import employee data ensuring PDPA (GDPR) compliance.

steps.title: Training & Go-Live
steps.description: Train HR staff and roll out self-service portal to employees.

items.title: Local vs Global
items.text: Local providers like HeRMeS (TechnoLogica) dominate due to strong compliance features.

items.title: GDPR
items.text: Strict adherence to PDPA is critical; data residency is often a concern.

items.title: Integration
items.text: Seamless integration with payroll software (if separate) is a key requirement.

faqs.question: Is digital signature supported?
faqs.answer: Yes, Qualified Electronic Signatures (QES) are legally binding for HR documents.

faqs.question: Can we use Excel?
faqs.answer: Possible for very small teams, but risky for compliance and data protection.

faqs.question: Do we need a DPO?
faqs.answer: Data Protection Officer may be required depending on the scale of processing.

items.title: Digital Labor File
items.text: Bulgaria is moving towards fully digital labor files (Dosie).

items.title: Language
items.text: Key HR documents must be available in Bulgarian.

items.title: Self-Service
items.text: Employee portals for leave requests and payslips are standard.

heroData.title: Accounting in Bulgaria
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Accounting in Bulgaria
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Accounting in Bulgaria.

steps.title: Setup
steps.description: Adopt National Chart of Accounts and define accounting policy (IFRS or NAS).

steps.title: Monthly Booking
steps.description: Process invoices, bank statements, and payroll; file VAT ledgers by the 14th.

steps.title: Closing
steps.description: Perform year-end closing entries and inventory reconciliation.

steps.title: Audit
steps.description: Conduct independent financial audit if criteria met (e.g., turnover > 8M BGN).

steps.title: Reporting
steps.description: Publish Annual Financial Statements (AFS) to Commercial Register by Sept 30.

items.title: SAF-T
items.text: Standard Audit File for Tax will be mandatory for large taxpayers starting 2026.

items.title: Audit Criteria 2024
items.text: Mandatory audit for small enterprises if 2 of 3 met: Assets > 4M BGN, Turnover > 8M BGN, Staff > 50.

items.title: Language
items.text: All primary accounting documents must be in Bulgarian and BGN.

faqs.question: Can we keep records abroad?
faqs.answer: Electronic records can be stored in the EU, but must be accessible to NRA upon request.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late AFS?
faqs.answer: Fines range from 0.1% to 0.5% of net sales revenue for the reporting period.

faqs.question: Is cash accounting allowed?
faqs.answer: Generally, accrual basis is required. Cash accounting is limited to specific VAT schemes.

items.title: NRA Connectivity
items.text: Fiscal devices (cash registers) must be connected to the NRA in real-time.

items.title: E-Invoicing
items.text: Widely used and encouraged, though not yet fully mandatory for B2B.

items.title: Currency
items.text: BGN is pegged to EUR (1.95583 BGN = 1 EUR), simplifying FX accounting.

steps.title: UBO Declaration
steps.description: Declare Ultimate Beneficial Owners in the Commercial Register (mandatory for all reporting entities).

steps.title: Annual Statistic Report
steps.description: Submit to the National Statistical Institute (NSI) by April 30.

steps.title: Tax Return
steps.description: File Annual Tax Return (GDD) by March 31 of the following year.

steps.title: Financial Statements
steps.description: Publish Annual Financial Statements in the Commercial Register by Sept 30.

steps.title: H&S Declaration
steps.description: File annual Health and Safety declaration to Labor Inspectorate if changes occurred.

items.title: Whistleblowing
items.text: Mandatory internal reporting channels for companies with 50+ employees (Whistleblower Protection Act 2024).

items.title: GDPR & PDPA
items.text: Strict enforcement by CPDP. Local data protection officer (DPO) may be required for large scale processing.

items.title: AML Measures
items.text: Stricter AML checks for transactions over BGN 30,000. Cash payments capped at BGN 10,000.

faqs.question: Is a local director required?
faqs.answer: No, a local resident director is not mandatory, but a contact person for tax authorities may be needed.

faqs.question: What is the cash limit?
faqs.answer: Cash payments between companies or individuals are limited to BGN 10,000 (approx €5,100).

faqs.question: Do we need a physical office?
faqs.answer: A registered address is mandatory. A virtual office is legally accepted for registration.

items.title: Digital Administration
items.text: Most government filings (NRA, Commercial Register) must be done electronically with a QES.

items.title: Labor Inspectorate
items.text: Conducts regular checks on employment contracts and workplace safety.

items.title: Translation
items.text: Official documents submitted to authorities must be in Bulgarian (sworn translation required).

steps.title: Registration
steps.description: Automatic tax registration upon incorporation; separate VAT registration required if turnover > BGN 100k.

steps.title: Advance Payments
steps.description: Monthly or quarterly advance CIT payments based on forecasted profit.

steps.title: Annual Filing
steps.description: File Annual Tax Return by March 31 of the following year.

steps.title: VAT Filing
steps.description: Monthly VAT returns filed by the 14th of the following month.

steps.title: Dividend Tax
steps.description: Deduct and pay 5% withholding tax on dividends distributed to individuals.

items.title: Global Min Tax
items.text: Top-up tax to 15% applies for large multinational groups (Pillar 2 rules) from 2024.

items.title: Treaty Network
items.text: Bulgaria has Double Tax Treaties (DTT) with over 70 countries reducing withholding rates.

items.title: Electronic Services
items.text: Non-resident suppliers of B2C digital services must register for VAT (OSS scheme available).

faqs.question: When is VAT mandatory?
faqs.answer: Upon reaching BGN 100,000 turnover in 12 consecutive months. Voluntary registration is possible anytime.

faqs.question: Are there tax incentives?
faqs.answer: Yes, for investments in high unemployment regions and R&D activities.

faqs.question: How are crypto assets taxed?
faqs.answer: Gains from trading are generally taxed as personal income (10%) or corporate profit.

items.title: Lowest in EU
items.text: Bulgaria maintains one of the lowest flat tax rates (10%) in the European Union.

items.title: Deadlines
items.text: Strict adherence to the 14th of the month VAT deadline is crucial to avoid fines.

items.title: Social Security Cap
items.text: Social security contributions are capped at a monthly income of BGN 3,750 (2024).

heroData.title: Legal Framework
heroData.subtitle: Navigating contracts and employment law in Bulgaria
heroData.description: Expert legal support for MSAs, employment contracts, and corporate law.

steps.title: Drafting
steps.description: Prepare bilingual MSA and employment contracts complying with Bulgarian Obligations and Contracts Act.

steps.title: Localization
steps.description: Ensure clauses like non-compete and IP transfer are enforceable under local labor code.

steps.title: Review
steps.description: Legal review by local counsel (e.g., Wolf Theiss, Dimitrov, Petrov & Co).

steps.title: Execution
steps.description: Sign with Qualified Electronic Signature (QES) or wet ink.

steps.title: Notarization
steps.description: Required for specific transactions (e.g., real estate, share transfers) but not for standard commercial MSAs.

items.title: Top Firms
items.text: Leading firms include Dimitrov, Petrov & Co, Djingov, Gouginski, Kyutchukov & Velichkov (DGKV), and Wolf Theiss.

items.title: Right to Disconnect
items.text: 2024 Labor Code amendments introduce the right to disconnect for remote workers.

items.title: Remote Work
items.text: Employment contracts must now specify the exact remote workplace location(s).

faqs.question: Are non-competes enforceable?
faqs.answer: Difficult to enforce for employees post-termination unless specific compensation is paid.

faqs.question: Is English law accepted?
faqs.answer: For B2B MSAs, yes. For employment contracts, Bulgarian Labor Code is mandatory.

faqs.question: Can we sign digitally?
faqs.answer: Yes, QES (DocuSign with QES add-on, Evrotrust) is legally equivalent to a handwritten signature.

items.title: Notice Periods
items.text: Standard notice is 1-3 months, mutually agreed in the contract.

items.title: Probation
items.text: Maximum probation period is 6 months; must be explicitly stated.

items.title: Termination
items.text: Bulgaria is pro-employee; termination 'at will' does not exist. Specific grounds are required.

heroData.title: Tech Hub of the Balkans
heroData.subtitle: Access world-class engineering talent in Bulgaria
heroData.description: Top-rated software development companies and R&D centers in Sofia, Plovdiv, and Varna.

steps.title: Discovery
steps.description: Define tech stack (Java, .NET, Python common) and engagement model (Staff Aug vs. Project).

steps.title: Vendor Selection
steps.description: Evaluate top providers like Dreamix, Accedia, Mentormate, or Scalefocus.

steps.title: Team Composition
steps.description: Interview key engineers; verified English proficiency is high.

steps.title: Contracting
steps.description: Sign MSA with clear IP assignment clauses ensuring client ownership.

steps.title: Kickoff
steps.description: Agile sprint planning; typically GMT+2 timezone alignment with Europe.

items.title: Key Hubs
items.text: Sofia is the primary hub (80%+ of industry), followed by Plovdiv and Varna.

items.title: Talent Quality
items.text: Strong tradition in mathematics and engineering. consistently high rankings in Olympiads.

items.title: Cost Efficiency
items.text: Operating costs for R&D centers are significantly lower than Western Europe.

faqs.question: Who owns the code?
faqs.answer: Under Bulgarian law, works for hire belong to the employer/client if specified in the contract.

faqs.question: What is the time difference?
faqs.answer: Bulgaria is in the EET (UTC+2) / EEST (UTC+3) zone, aligning well with Europe and overlapping US East Coast morning.

faqs.question: Are developers fluent in English?
faqs.answer: Yes, English is the standard business language in the IT sector (B2/C1 level is common).

items.title: Blue Cards
items.text: Streamlined EU Blue Card process for non-EU IT specialists.

items.title: Infrastructure
items.text: Bulgaria has some of the fastest internet speeds in the world.

items.title: Attrition
items.text: Market is competitive; retention strategies (benefits, flexible work) are crucial.

heroData.title: Digital Marketing
heroData.subtitle: Grow your brand with top Bulgarian agencies
heroData.description: Expertise in SEO, PPC, Social Media, and Creative Design.

steps.title: Agency Pitch
steps.description: Review portfolios of top agencies like eDesign, Xplora BG, or Metrix Digital.

steps.title: Localization Strategy
steps.description: Adapt messaging for local nuances; distinct differences between Sofia and countryside.

steps.title: Channel Selection
steps.description: Focus on Facebook/Instagram (dominant), Google Ads, and increasingly TikTok.

steps.title: Influencer Outreach
steps.description: Engage local micro-influencers for authentic brand endorsement.

steps.title: Performance Tracking
steps.description: Set clear KPIs (CPA, ROAS) and review monthly reports.

items.title: Social Media
items.text: Facebook is the absolute leader. LinkedIn is vital for B2B.

items.title: E-commerce
items.text: Cash on Delivery (COD) is still popular, though card payments are growing fast.

items.title: GDPR
items.text: Marketing databases must be strictly GDPR compliant (opt-in mandatory).

faqs.question: Is English content enough?
faqs.answer: For B2C, no. Bulgarian language content is essential for trust and conversion.

faqs.question: What are the ad tax rules?
faqs.answer: Digital services (ads) from non-EU entities (like Meta/Google US) may trigger reverse charge VAT.

faqs.question: Do I need a local website?
faqs.answer: A .bg domain builds trust, but a localized .com is generally sufficient.

items.title: Viber
items.text: Viber is widely used for messaging and brand channels in Bulgaria.

items.title: Events
items.text: In-person events and conferences are rebounding strongly post-pandemic.

items.title: Video
items.text: Short-form video content is seeing the highest engagement rates.
